notes.summary: Primary-source audit preserves the distinctions between ordinary P-type, I-envelope mass, Cao current products and class numerical dimension; published lower-dimensional results require additional hypotheses.
notes.detailedSummary: The four permitted source versions and pertinent statements and proof bodies were read using literal LF coordinates. DRWNXZ provides class-level bodies and analytic partial bodies, not a general arbitrary-P numerical theorem. Xia’s zero-volume dimension equality remains conjectural, and its Chebyshev question concerns an auxiliary more-singular Kähler-current potential. Cao’s current product and line-bundle numerical definition have different domains. CHPW requires a projective positive-volume-subvariety flag.
notes.text:
This is a source audit and an explicit declaration of published background, not an independent proof of the published theorems.

The versions are DRWNXZ arXiv:2309.07584v3, 5 January 2026; Xia arXiv:2112.04290v2, 13 April 2024; Cao arXiv:1210.5692v1, 21 October 2012; and CHPW arXiv:1508.03922v5, header 5 February 2018 and internal date 24 September 2018. Their literal LF-split entry counts are respectively 2034, 2700, 1931 and 1425.

DRWNXZ LF 226–263 supplies the current-potential setup and potential-descent proof, initially under a standing big-class assumption. The exact classical inputs retained below are bounded-above psh removability across analytic sets and equality of canonical representatives agreeing almost everywhere. LF 314–333 gives rational divisorial subtraction, positivity via Siu decomposition, and preservation of analytic singularities through division of ideal generators. LF 338–385 defines gentle analytic singularities, including rational coefficients and smooth divisorial resolution. LF 561–620 specifies globally smooth connected complete flags, recursive generic-Lelong valuations and the big body as their Euclidean closure. LF 624–691 supplies big-class properties and the pseudoeffective perturbative intersection. LF 852–894 defines partial bodies for gentle analytic Kähler references and proves the divisorial identity. Definition 2.12, LF 494–502, assigns zero volume to nonbig classes and otherwise takes the supremum of gentle-current top masses. The ambient-volume theorem and proof are LF 1389–1415, with pertinent reduction and induction bodies also extracted at LF 939–963 and 1139–1388. None supplies the general arbitrary-P lower-dimensional theorem.

Xia LF 67–105 uses projective line-bundle sections and multiplier ideals. LF 371–429 distinguishes ordinary P, C and I-envelopes. Proposition 2.10 identifies C with P only under positive actual input top mass. Theorem 2.19, LF 476–494, computes section volume from I-envelope mass, not unconditionally from the input current. LF 1158–1185 records I-invariance. LF 1623–1637 labels the zero-volume dimension equality Conjecture 5.29. LF 1824–1840 concerns an auxiliary more-singular Kähler-current potential eta, not an arbitrary positive form.

Cao LF 162–166 states the global quasi-psh potential representation for positive currents on compact Kähler manifolds. Definitions 2–3 and the comparison proof, LF 172–279, define cohomological current products through quasi-equisingular approximants and their absolutely continuous parts. Definition 4, LF 281–289, concerns line-bundle metrics. Only Definition 3 is applied to the transcendental smooth currents below. The projective hypersurface reduction, LF 660–721, cannot supply a curve on a curve-free torus.

CHPW LF 166–185 states Theorem B; LF 530–577 defines positive volume subvarieties. LF 915–1085 contains the relevant restricted-series and flag-slice proofs. Their numerical theorem requires a smooth projective variety, a pseudoeffective real divisor and a flag containing a positive volume subvariety. LF 1090–1096 permits smaller dimension for other flags. These results are not applied to the torus.

The literal extracts are in source-extracts/source-provenance.json; application hypotheses are in source-application-ledger.json. Rerun python3 prepare_sources.py. Provenance checks do not certify mathematical correctness.

notes.summary: A reconstructed dense-null-leaf torus has a genuinely transcendental rank-one class, only constant beta-psh potentials, and numerical/actual/Cao current degree one; rigidity persists on every smooth Kähler model.
notes.detailedSummary: A Baire construction gives a complex two-torus with no nonzero integral (1,1)-classes. Fourier averaging proves density of suitably chosen complex-line leaves. A constant semipositive form with that kernel has square zero and positive Kähler pairing. Subharmonic Liouville and upper semicontinuity prove potential rigidity. Nonbig descent extends it to every smooth compact Kähler model. Every model curve is contracted, so no positive one-dimensional complex carrier exists. This is a restricted deductive draft, not a general P-type construction.
notes.text:
Use dd^c=i partial-barpartial/(2 pi). The following is an unverified deductive proof, not numerical evidence.

Vary a linear complex structure J on R^4 in a connected component of oriented complex structures. Integral torus H^2 consists of integral alternating forms e. Translation averaging preserves class and type and gives the constant representative, so e has type (1,1) precisely when e(Jv,Jw)=e(v,w). Each nonzero integral e imposes a proper real-analytic condition: choose v1,v3 with e(v1,v3) nonzero, complete to an oriented basis v1,v2,v3,v4, and positively rescale v2 until e(v2,v4) differs. The complex structure pairing v1 with v2 and v3 with v4 violates invariance. This works in either orientation component. The identity principle and Baire’s theorem therefore allow avoidance of all countably many loci. The resulting M=(R^4,J)/Z^4 is Kähler through any constant positive compatible Hermitian form. A curve would have a nonzero integral (1,1)-class, detected by its positive Kähler area, so M has no curves and its divisor-class span is zero.

Choose a complex line W avoiding the kernels of all nonzero integral real characters. For each character k, the excluded line is the complex kernel of k-i kJ, so only countably many points of CP^1 are excluded. To prove density, average characters over x+sw+tJw, s,t in [-R,R]. Every nonzero character has at least one nonzero frequency on this plane, and its normalized average tends to zero as a product of sinc factors. Trigonometric approximation gives convergence of continuous-function averages to Haar integrals. A positive bump supported in any nonempty open set has positive integral, so every affine W-leaf enters that set.

Let ell be a nonzero complex-linear functional with kernel W and beta a positive constant multiple of i d ell wedge d bar ell. Then beta is smooth, closed, semipositive, rank one, beta^2=0, and integral beta wedge omega_M>0. Its nonzero class alpha is genuinely transcendental. It is nef because beta+epsilon omega_M is Kähler. A Kähler current T in alpha satisfying T>=delta omega_M would yield 0=integral T wedge beta>=delta integral omega_M wedge beta>0. Hence alpha is nonbig and has zero class volume independently of any input-current mass.

A bounded-above nontrivial subharmonic function on C is constant: Jensen’s formula makes any positive Laplacian mass force logarithmically growing circular means; therefore its Laplacian is zero. The differentiated Poisson formula on arbitrarily large discs then makes all harmonic derivatives zero. For phi beta-psh on M, compactness bounds phi above. Its restriction to a null leaf is subharmonic or identically minus infinity because beta restricts to zero. Choose a finite-value point. Liouville makes phi constant c on its dense leaf. Upper semicontinuity gives phi>=c everywhere, hence finiteness everywhere. Each leaf now has a constant restriction, and density compares any two constants in both directions. Thus PSH(M,beta)=R. The global potential representation in n1 proves uniqueness of beta among positive currents in alpha. The ordinary envelope is P_beta[0]=0.

For any proper bimeromorphic pi:X->M with smooth compact Kähler source, a pi^*beta-psh potential descends on the isomorphism locus and remains bounded above. Add local beta potentials and apply the exact removability input in n1 across the analytic exceptional image. The extended function pulls back to the original potential off an analytic set, then everywhere by equality of canonical representatives. This reconstructs descent without bigness. Consequently PSH(X,pi^*beta)=R and pi^*beta is the unique positive current in pi^*alpha.

Every smooth compact model curve Y is contracted. Its pushed integration current pi_*[Y] is closed positive of type (1,1), by holomorphic pullback of test forms and Stokes. Its class is integral, from the pushed integral fundamental class. Translation averaging gives a constant integral (1,1)-representative on M, which must vanish. If pi|Y were nonconstant, integral_Y pi^*omega_M would be positive, contradicting that zero class. Thus pi(Y) is a point and pi^*beta|Y=0. Flags on models exist: blow up a point and use its exceptional P^1. Kählerness follows from the cutoff-log construction: a sufficiently small logarithmic coefficient controls negative curvature on the cutoff annulus; after pullback and exceptional subtraction the normal pullback form and tangential Fubini–Study term have complementary positive directions.

The nef intersection numerical dimension is one, since beta^2=0 but beta has positive pairing with every Kähler form. Comparability of Kähler forms proves independence of that integer. The actual smooth nonpluripolar products are beta and beta^2=0. The constant potential sequence zero satisfies every Cao approximation condition, with all multiplier ideals equal to O; Definition 3 gives [beta] and [beta^2]=0. Their largest nonzero degrees are separately one, also upstairs. No general identification of these notions or line-bundle theorem is claimed.

A continuous Hausdorff-valued map constant on leaves is constant globally, because the closed fiber containing one dense leaf is all of M. This excludes a positive-dimensional Hausdorff leaf quotient, but does not exclude measured or other enriched carriers. The complete proof is in Sections 3–5 of P15.3-argument.md and P15.3-paper.tex.

notes.summary: Every usual unrescaled current-valuation limiting body on every fixed smooth Kähler model and complete flag of this torus is a point, despite numerical degree one.
notes.detailedSummary: The first divisorial valuation tends uniformly to zero by bounded-current compactness and uniqueness of the smooth limiting current. The second coordinate is bounded by the residual positive curve degree and also tends uniformly to zero. Smooth references contain the origin and impose an automatic ordinary type-zero constraint. The result holds for all fixed models and flags and positive smooth perturbation paths. It obstructs only constructions agreeing with these positive-level bodies and taking unrescaled limits.
notes.text:
Fix pi:X->M, a globally smooth connected complete flag X superset Y superset {q}, and a Kähler form Omega. Put beta_X=pi^*beta and xi_epsilon=pi^*alpha+epsilon[Omega]. These classes are Kähler. For each generating gentle analytic Kähler current G set t=nu(G,Y), S=G-t[Y], and a=nu(S|Y,q). Rational divisorial subtraction from n1 makes S positive analytic; zero generic Lelong number along Y makes its restriction a positive curve current. The valuation is (t,a).

Let f(epsilon) be the supremum of these first coordinates. Their trace masses equal integral (beta_X+epsilon Omega) wedge Omega and are bounded for epsilon<=1. G>=t[Y] bounds t by that mass divided by integral_Y Omega>0. Suppose f(epsilon) failed to tend to zero. Select epsilon_i->0 and G_i with t_i>=c>0. Bounded trace masses give a weakly convergent subsequence: local positive-current coefficient measures have total variations controlled by diagonal trace mass, and finite-measure weak compactness followed by a finite-cover diagonal selection supplies convergence. Positivity, type and closedness survive. Pairing with smooth closed complementary forms preserves the limiting class pi^*alpha. By n2 its positive-current limit is the unique smooth beta_X.

After another subsequence t_i->t>=c. Positivity of G_i-t_i[Y] would give beta_X>=t[Y]. Their Omega-trace measures contradict this: the smooth left side gives zero mass to Y, while the right gives t integral_Y Omega>0. Therefore f(epsilon)->0 uniformly over generating currents, without asserting continuity of generic Lelong numbers.

Put b=integral_Y Omega>0 and h=Y^2. A positive current on the compact curve is a positive measure, and its Lelong number at q is its atom in the specified normalization. Using pi^*alpha.Y=0 from n2 gives
0<=a<=integral_Y S|Y=epsilon b-th<=epsilon b+|h|f(epsilon).
No sign assumption on h is needed. The body therefore lies in [0,f(epsilon)] x [0,epsilon b+|h|f(epsilon)]. The smooth current beta_X+epsilon Omega has valuation (0,0), so every body contains the origin. Its Hausdorff distance to that point tends to zero by the displayed rectangle bound. The intersection over all epsilon>0 is exactly {(0,0)}.

The smooth reference has potential zero. Every quasi-psh potential on compact X is bounded above, so the ordinary more-singular constraint v<=0+C_v is automatic. Thus the positive-level partial body equals the full body and uses the prescribed ordinary smooth P-type from n2. For any smooth closed Kähler forms rho_j tending uniformly to zero, the same compactness argument makes first coordinates tend uniformly to zero; the second bound replaces epsilon b by integral_Y rho_j->0. The same point is the Hausdorff limit.

The quantification is over every individually fixed model and flag, not uniformly over moving models or flags. Nonpositive paths and coordinate rescaling are outside the result.

Consequently the following requirements are incompatible: include this datum; agree with these usual positive-level analytic-current partial bodies; define the zero-volume body by their unrescaled intersection or Hausdorff limit; and assert dimension equality with any of the three degrees computed as one in n2. Every allowed fixed flag instead gives affine dimension zero. This is stronger than one bad-flag example. It does not refute Xia’s projective conjecture and does not exclude all richer geometric constructions. Sections 6 and 8 of P15.3-argument.md contain the full proof and exact axioms.

notes.summary: The exact perturbative area exposes a reference scale; isotropic rescaling neither supplies a proved dimension-one carrier nor yields uncorrected reference independence.
notes.detailedSummary: The area is epsilon A_Omega+epsilon^2 B_Omega/2, where A_Omega=integral beta_X wedge Omega>0. Isotropic epsilon^(-1/2) dilation has area tending to A_Omega, without proved compactness or shape convergence. Any compact convex limit would be two-dimensional. Scaling Omega by c scales any such limit by sqrt(c). This is a conditional obstruction for that rescaling, not a general impossibility theorem.
notes.text:
For a fixed model and flag define A_Omega=integral_X beta_X wedge Omega>0 and B_Omega=integral_X Omega^2>0. Since beta_X^2=0, the positive-level Kähler self-intersection is 2 epsilon A_Omega+epsilon^2 B_Omega.

Its class volume equals this self-intersection directly in the definition from n1. A gentle analytic Kähler current resolves as a smooth semipositive residual gamma plus an effective rational divisor D. Smoothness and positivity off D imply semipositivity everywhere. Its nonpluripolar square downstairs and gamma^2 upstairs have equal integrals by locality and absence of mass on the omitted analytic sets. If eta is the pulled-back smooth Kähler representative, [eta]-[gamma]=[D], and integral eta^2-integral gamma^2=D.([eta]+[gamma])>=0 by semipositivity along divisor components. The smooth representative attains the upper bound. The published surface volume theorem then gives
2 Area Delta(xi_epsilon)=2 epsilon A_Omega+epsilon^2 B_Omega.

Hence Area(epsilon^(-1/2) Delta(xi_epsilon))->A_Omega. This identity proves neither boundedness nor Hausdorff convergence of those rescaled bodies. If a compact convex Hausdorff limit existed, continuity of area would make it positive-area and therefore two-dimensional. Area continuity follows from membership-indicator convergence outside the convex boundary in a common bounded box; empty-interior limits instead have arbitrarily small-area neighborhoods.

Reference dependence is exact:
epsilon^(-1/2) Delta(pi^*alpha+epsilon[c Omega])=sqrt(c) (c epsilon)^(-1/2) Delta(pi^*alpha+c epsilon[Omega]).
Thus any positive-area limit for c Omega would be sqrt(c) times the limit for Omega, with area c A_Omega. It cannot be unchanged when c!=1.

A positive pairing A_Omega could be declared as a reference or made one by rescaling the reference form. That divides by a positive lower-degree quantity, not by zero top mass. It still proves neither equality for different forms with the same pairing nor an anisotropic geometric carrier or arbitrary-P retention. No numerical interval is presented as an Okounkov body. Other rescalings and enriched carriers remain possible but unconstructed. Section 7 of P15.3-argument.md gives the full argument.
